source_schema.method: The server-to-client message set was read from the page above. It publishes these server messages: ready, timestamps, flush_complete, reset_complete and error; `finish` is published there as a CLIENT-to-server message, not a server one. This frame therefore does NOT conform to a documented server message — see notes. No vendor example payload, prose or field description was copied into this repository.

notes: REPORTED DRIFT, NOT SILENTLY WORKED AROUND. LmntSpeechSynthesizer terminates the stream on a server text frame whose `type` is `finish`, and SynthesizeAsync_ShouldTerminate_WhenServerSendsFinish asserts exactly that, so the fake must keep sending it. But `finish` does not appear in LMNT's published server-message enumeration (ready / timestamps / flush_complete / reset_complete / error); the docs list `finish` as a message the CLIENT sends to close its half. Either the SDK terminates on a message LMNT never sends — in which case the real stream ends only by close or timeout and this test proves nothing about the vendor — or LMNT echoes it undocumented. Only a capture can settle it, and LMNT is not-cleared, so this fixture records the frame the SDK actually needs and states the discrepancy here rather than papering over it. The alternative — adding the documented `ready` frame or replacing `finish` — was rejected because it would change how the fake answers rather than where its payload comes from (tasks.md 6.4). LmntServerNotification models `type`, `error` and `message`; of those the documented `error` message is the only overlap, and `message` appears in no documented LMNT server payload. What this artifact is worth: a documented schema is what the vendor says it sends, whereas a capture is what it actually sent on one day. Re-read the source_schema URL first when this suite starts failing; the page publishes no revision marker.
